short: Alexander the Great's first major victory over the Persian king Darius III, securing southern Anatolia.
full:
In November 333 BCE, the Macedonian army under Alexander the Great clashed with the main Persian army, commanded personally by King Darius III, near the mouth of the Pinarus River in southern Anatolia. Despite being significantly outnumbered, Alexander took advantage of the narrow coastal plain which prevented the Persians from fully deploying their numerical superiority. A swift and brutal Macedonian cavalry charge across the river shattered the Persian left flank.

The breakthrough forced Darius to flee the battlefield in a panic, abandoning his family and his royal treasure camp to the Macedonians. The victory at Issus opened the route to Syria and Egypt for Alexander, fundamentally weakening the Persian Empire and demonstrating the tactical brilliance of the Macedonian military machine.
